purpose: Flag likely modern Standard Estonian morphological leakage in intended Leivu text while respecting Leivu apocope, palatalization, and academic UPA/practical spellings.

rules.message: Looks like Standard Estonian active past participle -nud. Leivu uses South Estonian participle endings (-nu/-nü/-n/-nU or apocopated forms), not -nud.
rules.hint: Rewrite with authentic Leivu participle morphology rather than Estonian -nud.

rules.message: Looks like Standard Estonian passive past participle -tud/-dud. Leivu uses -t/-d or -tu/-tü/-du/-dü.
Looks like Standard Estonian past negation ei + -nud/-tud. Leivu uses past negation es + verb (es tie, es ole).
Standard Estonian contracted negation pole/polnud/poleks/polevat is foreign to Leivu.
May be Standard Estonian 3sg present -b. Leivu 3sg present typically ends vowel-stem or -s (or apocopated), rather than -b.
rules.hint: Verify against attested Leivu verb forms.

rules.message: Looks like Standard Estonian 3pl present -vad. Leivu uses -vA/-sE plural forms.
rules.hint: Replace Estonian -vad with attested Leivu 3pl morphology.

rules.message: Looks like Standard Estonian impersonal -takse/-dakse. Leivu uses -tAs/-dAs or South Estonian impersonal forms.
Looks like Standard Estonian conditional -ksin/-ksime/-ksite. Leivu uses South Estonian -ssi/-si conditional forms.
Looks like Standard Estonian illative -sse. Leivu illative uses -he, -de/-te, or short/geminate stem illatives.
rules.hint: Replace Estonian -sse with attested Leivu illative morphology.

rules.message: Looks like Standard Estonian plural illative -desse/-tesse.
Looks like Standard Estonian plural partitive -sid.
rules.hint: Check attested Leivu plural partitive forms (-sit/-it/-id or vowel plural).

rules.message: Looks like Standard Estonian -mas supine. Leivu supine inessive uses -mAn / -mAh / -məh.
May be Standard Estonian translative -ks. Leivu uses archaic -s (or -st) translative.
rules.hint: Use Leivu -s translative if this is an inflected noun/adjective.

do_not_flag_suffixes.reason: Glottal stop may be realized or lost under Latvian contact/apocope; never force a uniform spelling on historical sources.
